content:
Artificial Intelligence is transforming the way we create digital art. Whether you're an artist, content creator, game designer, or just a tech enthusiast, generating high-quality visuals based on descriptive prompts is now more intuitive and interactive than ever. In this blog post, we’ll walk through building a fully functional AI image generator using Streamlit, OpenAI’s DALL·E model, and custom theme/mood inputs to enrich your creative process.

🛠️ What We’re Building

We're creating a Streamlit web app that allows users to:

  • Input a custom prompt
  • Choose a theme (like "Cyberpunk" or "Fantasy")
  • Select a mood (like "Melancholic" or "Vibrant")
  • Pick an image size
  • Generate and download a unique AI-generated image

With just a few lines of Python code and OpenAI's API, you’ll be able to generate visually rich and emotionally resonant artwork in seconds.

📦 Tools & Libraries Used

import streamlit as st         # For building the UI
from openai import OpenAI     # OpenAI API for image generation
from PIL import Image         # To display and manipulate images
import requests               # For downloading generated images
import certifi, os            # Secure connection setup
from io import BytesIO        # Image buffering

🔐 API Key Setup

First, store your OpenAI API key securely in a file named apikey.py:

apikey = "your-openai-api-key"

Then use this to configure the environment:

os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = apikey
OpenAI.api_key = apikey
client = OpenAI()

🎨 Add Themes and Moods for Creative Flair

To make image generation more dynamic and expressive, we introduce predefined theme and mood options:

themes = ["Futuristic", "Mythological", "Medieval", "Surreal", "Romantic", "Sci-Fi", "Fantasy", "Cyberpunk"]
moods = ["Euphoric", "Melancholic", "Dark", "Vibrant", "Calm", "Tranquil", "Chaotic", "Mysterious"]

🖼️ Streamlit Interface

We design a simple UI with Streamlit to capture user input:

st.title("Advanced AI Image Generator with Theme-Based Variations")
prompt = st.text_input("Enter the image prompt:", "A futuristic city under the stars")
theme = st.selectbox("Select a theme:", themes)
mood = st.selectbox("Select a mood:", moods)
size = st.selectbox("Select image size:", ["1024x1024", "512x512", "256x256"])

🤖 Generating the Image

Once the "Generate Image" button is clicked, the app:

  1. Combines the inputs into a descriptive prompt
  2. Sends the prompt to OpenAI's image generation endpoint
  3. Retrieves the image and displays it
  4. Offers a download button
full_prompt = f"{prompt} in a {theme} theme with a {mood} mood"
response = client.images.generate(prompt=full_prompt, n=1, size=size)
image_url = response.data[0].url

Then we load and display the image using PIL and Streamlit:

img_response = requests.get(image_url, verify=certifi.where())
img = Image.open(BytesIO(img_response.content))
st.image(img, caption=f"Generated Image: {full_prompt}", use_column_width=True)

Finally, allow users to download the generated image:

img_bytes = BytesIO()
img.save(img_bytes, format="PNG")
st.download_button(label="Download Image", data=img_bytes, file_name=f"{theme.lower()}_{mood.lower()}.png", mime="image/png")

🚀 Why This App Stands Out

✅ Creative Control – Users can mix and match prompts, moods, and themes to get unique images
✅ Streamlit Simplicity – Fast UI creation with minimal boilerplate
✅ Secure API Integration – Uses OpenAI's official library securely
✅ User-Friendly Output – Inline display and downloadable image

💡 Use Cases

  • Concept Art Generation for writers and game developers
  • Mood Boards for designers
  • Educational Projects to visualize abstract concepts
  • Social Media Content tailored to aesthetic preferences

📌 Final Thoughts

This project bridges the gap between AI capabilities and human creativity. With a few simple inputs, anyone can generate art that resonates with emotion, atmosphere, and style. Try it, tweak it, and let your imagination run wild!

🔗 Ready to Try It?

Save the code in a file like ai_image_generator.py and run it with:

streamlit run ai_image_generator.py

✨ Don’t forget to replace apikey with your actual OpenAI key in apikey.py.

Python Code:

import os
import certifi
import streamlit as st
from openai import OpenAI
from apikey import apikey  # Store your OpenAI key in apikey.py
import requests
from PIL import Image
from io import BytesIO

# Set up the OpenAI API key
os.environ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] = apikey
OpenAI.api_key = apikey
client = OpenAI()

# Define themes and moods
themes = ["Futuristic", "Mythological", "Medieval", "Surreal", "Romantic", "Sci-Fi", "Fantasy", "Cyberpunk"]
moods = ["Euphoric", "Melancholic", "Dark", "Vibrant", "Calm", "Tranquil", "Chaotic", "Mysterious"]

# Streamlit UI setup
st.title("Advanced AI Image Generator with Theme-Based Variations")
st.write("Create AI-generated images based on themes and moods. Select a theme and mood to enrich your image generation.")

# User input: Prompt, Theme, Mood, and Image Size
prompt = st.text_input("Enter the image prompt:", "A futuristic city under the stars")
theme = st.selectbox("Select a theme:", themes)
mood = st.selectbox("Select a mood:", moods)
size = st.selectbox("Select image size:", ["1024x1024", "512x512", "256x256"])

if st.button("Generate Image"):
    # Combine the inputs into a full prompt
    full_prompt = f"{prompt} in a {theme} theme with a {mood} mood"
    st.write(f"Generating image for: '{full_prompt}'")

    # Generate the image
    response = client.images.generate(prompt=full_prompt, n=1, size=size)
    image_url = response.data[0].url

    # Fetch and display the image
    img_response = requests.get(image_url, verify=certifi.where())
    img = Image.open(BytesIO(img_response.content))

    st.image(img, caption=f"Generated Image: {full_prompt}", use_column_width=True)

    # Provide an option to download the image
    img_bytes = BytesIO()
    img.save(img_bytes, format="PNG")
    img_bytes.seek(0)
    st.download_button(label="Download Image", data=img_bytes, file_name=f"{theme.lower().replace(' ', '_')}_{mood.lower()}.png", mime="image/png")
